---
title: "A10: Drugs used in diabetes"
description: "ATC A10 drugs used in diabetes for modelers: hbA1c is not an E~max~ on concentration; long trials drift; clamp readouts."
date: "2026-02-08"
---

The disease these drugs treat is covered in the [diabetes primer](/docs/pathology-primers/diabetes/).

**Endpoint.**
HbA1c, glycated hemoglobin, is the most commonly used biomarker of glycemic management and a surrogate endpoint for anti-diabetic drug approval [@lledogarciaSemimechanisticModelRelationship2013].

**HbA1c is not an E~max~ on concentration.**
It accumulates by glycation over the red cell lifespan, so it lags mean glucose and is written as a transformation of the glucose profile, not as a drug effect [@lledogarciaSemimechanisticModelRelationship2013; @hamrenModelsPlasmaGlucose2008].

**Typical structure.**
Provocations (OGTT, IVGTT) need the glucose-insulin feedback loop stated explicitly, and integrated models carrying both species have been built for intravenous and for oral provocation data [@silberIntegratedModelGlucose2007; @jauslinIntegratedGlucoseInsulin2007].

**Long trials drift.**
Type 2 diabetes progresses under treatment, so comparing drugs over a year needs disease progression on beta cell function and insulin sensitivity, not a fixed baseline [@dewinterMechanismbasedDiseaseProgression2006].

**Clamp readouts.**
Insulin degludec was profiled by the glucose infusion rate of a euglycemic clamp, a [pharmacodynamic](/docs/concepts/pd/) readout: in 65 healthy men, body mass index was inversely correlated with the 24 hour GIR AUC [@liEffectBMIPharmacokinetic2023].
